subject: general
question: India's first indigenous satellite launch vehicle is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**SLV–3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Satellite Launch Vehicle-3 (SLV-3) was the first satellite launch vehicle developed by India.
 
• SLV-3 was developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) under the guidance of Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
 
• The first successful launch of SLV-3 took place on July 18, 1980, which placed the Rohini satellite into orbit, making India the sixth country to have satellite launch capabilities.
 
• The development of SLV-3 was a significant milestone in India's space program, marking the beginning of indigenous satellite launch capabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ASLV (Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle)**

 
 
• ASLV was designed to augment payload capacity compared to SLV-3.
 
• It was used to place satellites into low Earth orbit (LEO).
 
• ASLV had a mixed record of success and was eventually phased out in favor of more advanced launch vehicles.
 
 
 
• **GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle)**
 
 
• GSLV is designed to launch heavier payloads into geostationary orbits.
 
• It uses a cryogenic upper stage, which enhances its payload capacity.
 
• GSLV is crucial for launching communication satellites.
 
 
 
• **PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle)**
 
 
• PSLV is known for its reliability and versatility.
 
• It is used to launch satellites into polar orbits and geostationary transfer orbits.
 
• PSLV has been instrumental in launching numerous Indian and foreign satellites.
